name: @appstrate/ssh-mcp
description: Reach one host over SSH. Shells out to the `ssh` / `sftp` clients baked into the bun runner image; the private key is delivered to this process as a file and never enters the agent container. There is no free-form command tool: `ssh_exec` sends the NAME of a verb from a closed allowlist, and the target's own `command=` dispatcher decides what that name means. Host-key pinning is mandatory — the connection carries the host's public key and `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` refuses anything else; there is no trust-on-first-use. Read and write are separate tools so a host can grant one without the other.
author: Appstrate

tools.name: ssh_probe
tools.description: Connect, verify the pinned host key and authenticate, then report the effective policy (host, user, allowed verbs, read-only, how the host was reached). Executes nothing on the target and returns no remote data.

tools.name: ssh_exec
tools.description: Run ONE pre-declared verb on the remote host. `verb` must be a name from the connection's allowlist; the bare name is what crosses the wire and the target's forced-command dispatcher resolves it. Arbitrary shell commands are not accepted.

tools.name: ssh_read_file
tools.description: Read a remote file over SFTP (256 KiB cap, truncation flagged). Read-only — works against a target restricted to `internal-sftp -R`.

tools.name: ssh_list_dir
tools.description: List a remote directory over SFTP. Entries are returned sorted by name. Read-only.

tools.name: ssh_write_file
tools.description: Write a remote file over SFTP. Mutating — withhold this tool from an agent that must not write, and back that up with a read-only account on the target. Refused outright when the connection is marked read-only.
